draft.title: Persuasive techniques
card: a question asked for effect, not for an answer. It makes the reader think the answer is obvious, such as "Who wants to swim in a dirty river?"
words such as we, us and our. They place the writer and reader on the same side, such as "We can keep our beaches clean."
words chosen to stir a feeling, such as "heartbreaking" or "disgusting". They make the reader feel, not only think.
Repetition says a word or phrase again to make it stick. Expert opinion names a person with knowledge of the topic, such as a doctor, so the claim seems more trustworthy.
draft.remember: Persuasive techniques work on the reader's thinking, feelings and trust to win them over.

a.q: A flyer says: "Together, we can make our town safer." Which technique does this show?
a.why: The words together, we and our place the writer and reader on the same side, which is inclusive language. It is not a rhetorical question because nothing is asked.
a.clue: Look at the small words that mean the writer and reader together.

b.q: Mia writes in a school newsletter that Dr Lee, a dentist for 20 years, says fizzy drinks harm teeth. Which technique mainly makes her claim seem believable?
b.why: Naming Dr Lee and her 20 years as a dentist shows she has knowledge, so readers trust the claim. Nothing in Mia's sentence is chosen to stir a feeling, so emotive words are not the cause.
b.clue: Who is speaking, and why should we trust them?
